category_title: High school students with learning disabilities and ADHD who struggle to break down multi-step algebraic tasks
scenario_title: Resistance to transitioning from concrete manipulatives to abstract notation
minimal_context: The student and tutor are working one-on-one to multiply linear expressions, transitioning from using Algebra Lab Gear manipulatives to writing abstract symbols.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: You did well multiplying the last expression with the Algebra Lab Gear. For this next problem, let's move away from the blocks and try to solve it using only abstract symbols on your paper.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: But I like using these. I’m writing out my problem over here. I have an equation and I am breaking it up and multiplying because this is a multiplying bar and this is x and so I have x plus 3 so x plus 3 times, and this is timesing it, x plus 2 and that’s going to equal x squared.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: That is exactly what you did. Now, let's put the corner piece and the blocks aside and just write the numbers for the next one.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I think if it was broken down I would be able to do it. The problem is that there are a lot of steps and once I understand what to do with one part I forget the other – I guess I’m not good at blending the steps.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's just try to write it out with the numbers and see what happens.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: It’s so much more hard because it’s not broken up then. Like what I do is I see this (pointing to x-bar) and this (pointing to constant blocks) and I read it and I write it then I move it. And then it’s all broken up and I see the whole problem happening. But when it’s all numbers then I forgot where to break it up and what’s what.

task.content: Multiplying linear expressions and transitioning from concrete manipulatives to abstract notation
task.learning_goal: Moving away from the blocks to use only abstract symbols

context.materials: Algebra Lab Gear (ALG) manipulatives, constant blocks, x-bars, abstract symbols, graphic organizer (Box Method)

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When told that we were moving away from the blocks to use only abstract symbols
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Resisted giving up the manipulatives and complained that she forgot where to break the problem up
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Felt the task was 'so much more hard' because it was not broken up visually
related_quotes: It’s so much more hard because it’s not broken up then. Like what I do is I see this (pointing to x -bar) and this (pointing constant blocks) and I read it and I write it then I move it. And then it’s all broken up and I see the whole problem happening. But when it’s all numbers then I forgot where to break it up and what’s what.

behavior_patterns.condition: When presented with a word problem and table of data with a lot of words and steps
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Unable to develop a plan to engage in the tasks, scoring extremely low (0% - 4%) on pretests
behavior_patterns.internal_state: Felt unable to blend the steps together once she understood one part
related_quotes: I think if it was broken down I would be able to do it. The problem is that there are a lot of words and a lot of steps and once I understand what to do with one part I forget the other – I guess I’m not good at blending the steps.
